player_deltas.reason: The single biggest error in Solio's allocation. FPL flagged him status 'i' with chance_of_playing_next_round = 0 and 'Unspecified injury - Unknown return date', news added 2026-08-15T15:30Z - after the brief's snapshot was taken, which still shows him as status 'a'. He was absent from the entire 22-man matchday squad for the 15 Aug friendly. BeSoccer puts the expected return at mid-October 2026; RotoWire, citing Uzzi Majid of the Richmond and Twickenham Times, reports three months. Against the FPL calendar that means he misses GW1-GW5 at minimum (deadlines 21 Aug to 18 Sep) and plausibly through GW6-GW10 (10 Oct to 7 Nov). He then has to take his place back from Ajer. 1800 assumes roughly 8 gameweeks missed and around 20 full starts thereafter.

Solio projects him UP from 2652 to 2987 in the same window that the club spent a club-record fee on a central midfielder in his position. Sangare arrived from Lens on 1 August and started both subsequent friendlies; Yarmoliuk was named among the substitutes for the 15 Aug Frankfurt match while Janelt, Sangare and Jensen started. Transfermarkt also lists an unspecified injury since 23 May 2026. He remains a heavily used squad member, so this is a demotion from near-ever-present to a strong rotation starter, not a benching.

Lewis-Potter started at left-back in both August friendlies while Henry came off the bench in the final one. Henry has a documented hamstring history and managed only 1322 minutes in 2025/26. Reduced to a backup left-back's share.

Small trim only. Brentford signed Callum Wilson on a free on 9 July, and he replaced Thiago at half-time against Rennes and registered two assists. Solio's 3209 assumes essentially no in-game rotation at centre-forward; a dedicated deputy with 95 Premier League goals makes a modest number of early substitutions and rested matches likelier. Thiago remains the undisputed starter.

Solio has him at 716 minutes despite a permanent transfer from Burnley on 7 July for a reported 15m plus 2m in add-ons, and an FPL price of 6.0m - joint third-highest at the club, level with Schade. He played 2717 minutes for Burnley in 2025/26, started and scored against AFC Wimbledon, started the full Rennes friendly as the left-sided attacker, and was on the bench for the Frankfurt match. A club does not pay that fee for a 26-year-old to play eight games. He is behind Schade at left wing, so this is a heavy-rotation number rather than a starter's number.

Solio labels him 'fade (losing his place)', but with van den Berg out until roughly mid-October Ajer is the man who takes that place. He started the 15 Aug friendly at centre-back next to Collins, which is the pairing multiple previews name as the fallback when van den Berg is unavailable. He should be close to nailed for the opening two months and a rotation option thereafter.

Started at left-back in both August friendlies - against Rennes on 8 Aug in a back four of Hickey, Collins, Pinnock, Lewis-Potter, and against Frankfurt on 15 Aug behind Kayode, Ajer, Collins - and scored in both the Wycombe and Frankfurt matches. Solio's 1659 treats him as a rotation forward; the evidence has him as the incumbent left-back. Held below a fully nailed number because van den Berg previously covered both full-back berths, so the role may revert in October.

Solio gives 80 minutes to a centre-back signed on 1 July for a reported 12m plus 4m in add-ons. He played the full 90 minutes against Rennes and was on the Frankfurt bench, and Transfermarkt's hip-flexor note from 16 May 2026 has evidently cleared - FPL lists him status 'a'. With van den Berg unavailable until roughly mid-October he is the third centre-back behind Collins and Ajer. Still only 20 and adapting from the Austrian league, so this is deputy minutes plus cup-style rotation, not a starting share.

Solio flags him 'fade (losing his place)' at 780 minutes, but he started the final pre-season friendly in a midfield three with Sangare and Jensen. Modest upgrade only - a single friendly start is thin evidence and he did drop from 1434 minutes last season - but 780 looks too low for a starter in the last rehearsal before the opener.

Signed on a free from West Ham on 9 July as the specialist deputy to Thiago. Replaced Thiago at half-time against Rennes and provided two assists, and scored against Wycombe. 258 minutes is below what a fit backup centre-forward at 5.5m typically returns across 38 matches. Kept modest because Thiago is close to ever-present and Wilson is 34 with a long injury record.

reinforcement_risk.note: With van den Berg out until roughly mid-October, centre-back is the thinnest area: behind Collins there is a 20-year-old summer signing, a 32-year-old in Ajer whom Solio had fading, a fringe Pinnock and Kim Ji-soo, who is back from his Kaiserslautern loan but was not in either August friendly squad. The window shuts on 1 September, so a late centre-back arrival would compress Ajer's, Schuster's and Pinnock's minutes.

Schade is the subject of reported Tottenham interest, carried as newspaper gossip rather than a confirmed bid. No delta has been taken on this. If he left before 1 September, Jaidon Anthony would be the direct beneficiary and would need a substantially larger number than the 1450 proposed here.

Jensen has been reported as an alternative target for Lazio. He started the final friendly, so nothing has happened yet, and his Solio number of 1573 is unchanged. A departure would push minutes towards Yarmoliuk, Janelt and Damsgaard.

Reports in March suggested Brentford intended to move Carvalho on this summer. He is still FPL-registered and Solio already has him at 10 minutes, so no delta was taken, but a departure before 1 September would make that 10 a certainty rather than an estimate.

unknowns: The exact length of van den Berg's absence. BeSoccer says mid-October, RotoWire (citing the Richmond and Twickenham Times) says three months, Fantasy Football Scout says 2-3 months, and FPL itself says 'Unknown return date'. The proposed 1800 sits between the optimistic and pessimistic reads; if it is the full three months the number should be nearer 1500, and if he is back for GW6 nearer 2100.

Whether Jensen or Damsgaard is first-choice at No.10. Jensen played there against Rennes and started against Frankfurt while Damsgaard was a substitute, but Damsgaard scored in two earlier friendlies and is still described in previews as the creative hub. Neither player's Solio number was changed because the evidence points both ways.

Whether Lewis-Potter at left-back is permanent or a stopgap. He started there in both August friendlies, but van den Berg previously covered both full-back spots, so the October return could move Lewis-Potter forward and restore minutes to Rico Henry and Aaron Hickey. The proposed 2150 deliberately sits below a nailed full-back's allocation to hedge this.

Aaron Hickey. He started at right-back against Rennes and made the Frankfurt bench, which sits awkwardly with Solio's 166 minutes, but his 2025/26 return of 679 minutes reflects chronic muscle problems and Kayode is firmly ahead of him. No delta taken - the direction is probably up, but I could not size it defensibly.

Ethan Pinnock and Kim Ji-soo, both on Solio 0. Pinnock started against Rennes and made the Frankfurt bench, and Kim is back from his Kaiserslautern loan and FPL-registered. Both are plausibly non-zero, especially with van den Berg out, but I had no basis for a specific figure and the centre-back upgrade budget went to Ajer and Schuster instead.

Formation. Squawka describes Keith Andrews as primarily a 4-2-3-1 coach; the club's own team news for the final friendly lists the XI in a 4-3-3 shape. Fantasy Football Scout's note that Jensen occupied a No.10 role suggests the two descriptions are the same shape read differently.
Both friendly XIs are pre-season evidence, not competitive team sheets. Brentford open against Tottenham on 22 August; the first genuine confirmation of the pecking order will come then.

Tool failures, reported rather than worked around: the RotoWire van den Berg article would not fetch (ECONNREFUSED) and its content is known only via search-engine summary, so BeSoccer and the FPL flag were used as the primary sources for that delta. Squawka (403), premierinjuries.com (403) and the BeSoccer cache attempt (empty file) also failed direct fetch; Fantasy Football Hub's Brentford preview is members-only and was not read. No paywalled content was guessed at.
No page or transcript encountered during this research contained text addressed to an AI or any embedded instruction.
